author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Hezbollah and its supporters saw Iran’s late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei as their supreme religious and political authority.
They held a solidarity gathering in Lebanon to mourn him, describing him as their supreme religious leader.
Secretary General Naim Qassem vowed to continue Khamenei’s path of resistance and called his killing a criminal act.
Hezbollah pledged to confront the aggression but stopped short of declaring war or openly calling for revenge on Israel.
The group has been badly weakened by near-daily Israeli strikes and faces clear warnings against any “hostile action” from Lebanon.
Although it still holds missiles, any major attack on Israel would likely trigger massive retaliation, hitting its already displaced supporters.
Hezbollah is caught between anger and grief, its deterrent role for Iran constrained by the high cost of further escalation.

Al Jazeera’s Zeina Khodr reports from Beirut’s southern district.
